item.content:encoded:
Grassroots organizations working on urgent social justice campaigns, direct actions, accessibility initiatives, mutual aid, and community-led resistance can apply for the Resist Urgent Action Fund Grant 2026. The grant provides up to US$5,000 to eligible organizations that need timely financial support for urgent projects, campaigns, events, or programmatic activities.

The fund is designed to help frontline groups respond to immediate needs and emerging opportunities without being restricted by lengthy traditional funding processes. Resist prioritizes projects that reflect escalated resistance, organizing, campaigns, direct action, community events, accessibility, mutual aid, or other forms of grassroots movement-building.

The next application cycle is scheduled to run from September 14 to September 18, 2026. Since applications are accepted until the available funding cap is reached, interested organizations should confirm their eligibility and submit their applications as early as possible.

Overview of the Resist Urgent Action Fund Grant 2026

Resist is a foundation that supports grassroots movements working toward justice, liberation, and social change. Its grantmaking approach focuses on redistributing resources to frontline communities and organizations that are often excluded from conventional philanthropic funding.

For 2026, Resist has introduced changes to its grantmaking process to deepen its impact and provide more adaptive support to grantees. The Urgent Action Fund is intended for organizations facing urgent needs or pursuing timely opportunities that require immediate financial resources.

The fund can support a range of activities, including but not limited to:

  • Urgent community events.
  • Direct actions and demonstrations.
  • Accessibility-related costs.
  • Mutual aid initiatives.
  • Campaign activities.
  • Escalated resistance efforts.
  • Organizing projects.
  • Community-based programmatic work.
  • Other urgent projects connected to grassroots social justice movements.

The grant is not intended to function as a conventional long-term institutional grant. Instead, it is designed to provide flexible support when organizations need resources to act quickly.

Key Details of the Resist Urgent Action Fund Grant

Category Details
Opportunity Resist Urgent Action Fund Grant 2026
Funding organization Resist
Opportunity type Grant
Grant amount Up to US$5,000
Eligible applicants New and returning eligible 501(c)(3) or fiscally sponsored organizations
Organizational budget requirement Annual budget below US$150,000
Geographic focus United States
Application method Online application
Next application cycle September 14–18, 2026
Deadline September 18, 2026
Official grant page Resist Grants Open page
Application portal Resist online grant application portal

What Is the Resist Urgent Action Fund?

The Resist Urgent Action Fund is a funding stream for organizations that require financial support for urgent projects or requests. Unlike funding programmes that may focus primarily on long-term strategic planning or annual operating budgets, the Urgent Action Fund is structured to help groups respond to immediate circumstances and timely organizing needs.

According to Resist, applications will open on the last Monday and close on the following Friday of each month until the available funding cap has been reached. The organization also indicates that projects demonstrating escalated resistance, campaigns, events, projects, or programmatic work will receive priority.

The next listed application cycle is:

September 14–18, 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day if they are ready to apply because the fund may stop accepting applications once its funding limit has been reached.

Grant Amount

Successful applicants may receive up to:

US$5,000

The grant can help eligible organizations cover urgent costs associated with their organizing and movement-building activities. The source information does not specify that every successful applicant will automatically receive the full US$5,000. The amount awarded may depend on the application, the organization’s needs, the available funds, and the grantmaking process.

Potential uses may include costs connected to:

  • Community organizing.
  • Direct-action activities.
  • Campaign implementation.
  • Urgent events.
  • Accessibility arrangements.
  • Mutual aid efforts.
  • Community mobilization.
  • Organizing materials.
  • Timely programme activities.
  • Other urgent work aligned with Resist’s grantmaking priorities.

Applicants should explain clearly why the funding is needed urgently and how the proposed activities contribute to their broader organizing or movement-building work.

Who Can Apply for the Resist Urgent Action Fund?

The 2026 Urgent Action Fund is open to eligible organizations that meet Resist’s grantmaking requirements.

1. 501(c)(3) Organizations

Organizations with recognized 501(c)(3) nonprofit status may apply if they meet the remaining eligibility requirements.

The organization must be based in the United States, have an annual budget below US$150,000, and demonstrate that its work fits within Resist’s broader social justice and grassroots organizing framework.

2. Fiscally Sponsored Organizations

Organizations that do not have their own 501(c)(3) status may still apply if they operate under a qualifying fiscal sponsor.

A fiscal sponsor is an eligible nonprofit organization that provides administrative, legal, and financial oversight to a project or group that does not have independent tax-exempt status.

Resist confirms that organizations with fiscal sponsors may apply. Applicants should be prepared to provide accurate information about their fiscal sponsor and follow any requirements outlined in the application portal.

3. New and Returning Applicants

The fund is open to both:

  • New organizations applying to Resist for the first time.
  • Returning organizations that have previously received Resist funding.

Previous funding from Resist is not required for an organization to be considered for the Urgent Action Fund, provided that it meets the stated eligibility requirements.

4. Organizations with Budgets Below US$150,000

Eligible organizations must have annual budgets below US$150,000.

This requirement is intended to prioritize smaller grassroots groups and frontline organizations that may have limited access to traditional sources of funding.

Organizations with annual budgets of US$150,000 or more are not eligible under the stated criteria.

Geographic Eligibility

The Resist Urgent Action Fund is geographically focused on the United States.

To qualify, applicants must generally:

  • Be based in the United States.
  • Conduct their primary work within the United States.
  • Demonstrate that the proposed activity serves communities or movements within the United States.

Organizations whose primary work is outside the United States are not eligible under Resist’s grantmaking criteria. This means that international organizations, groups based in other countries, or applicants seeking funding for projects primarily implemented outside the United States should not assume that they qualify.

The opportunity is therefore not a worldwide grant programme, even though its themes may be relevant to social justice organizations in other regions.

Types of Work Resist Supports

Resist’s grantmaking is focused on grassroots organizing, community power, structural change, and movements for justice and liberation.

Organizations applying for the Urgent Action Fund should be able to explain how their work fits into a broader movement or organizing ecosystem.

Relevant work may include:

Grassroots Organizing

This includes community-led efforts that bring people together to address structural social, political, or economic problems. Grassroots organizing may involve coalition-building, community education, leadership development, mobilization, and collective action.

Direct Action

The fund may support urgent direct-action activities connected to progressive organizing campaigns. Examples could include organizing demonstrations, public actions, mobilization efforts, or other forms of nonviolent collective action.

Campaigns

Organizations conducting timely campaigns may be considered, particularly where the campaign responds to an urgent issue or reflects an escalated phase of organizing.

Applicants should explain:

  • What issue the campaign addresses.
  • Who is affected.
  • What action is being taken.
  • Why the activity is urgent.
  • How the campaign connects to the organization’s wider goals.

Accessibility

The fund may support accessibility-related needs that enable people to participate in organizing, events, campaigns, and movement activities.

Accessibility expenses may include arrangements that remove barriers for people with disabilities or others who require specific forms of support to participate meaningfully.

Mutual Aid

Urgent mutual aid activities may be eligible when they are connected to the organization’s movement work and meet Resist’s grant criteria.

Applicants should distinguish between mutual aid that is part of broader grassroots organizing and activities that function solely as general material assistance. Resist’s eligibility information indicates that it does not generally fund material aid campaigns as a standalone category.

Community and Cultural Organizing

Resist also supports work involving cultural organizing, community-led education, consciousness-raising, radical pedagogy, and other forms of movement-building.

Projects should demonstrate how the proposed work contributes to collective power, social transformation, or community-led resistance.

Resist’s General Grantmaking Criteria

In addition to the specific Urgent Action Fund requirements, applicants should consider Resist’s broader eligibility criteria.

Resist indicates that organizations aligned with its grantmaking approach generally demonstrate several of the following characteristics:

  1. Connection to a broader social justice ecosystemThe organization understands how its work relates to other groups, campaigns, communities, and movements working toward social change.
  2. Clear purpose within movements for social changeThe organization can explain its role, goals, strategies, and contribution to broader efforts for justice and liberation.
  3. Intersectional or cross-issue analysisThe organization recognizes that social problems are interconnected and addresses issues through an intersectional or cross-issue perspective.
  4. Work against structural oppressionResist’s stated criteria refer to work against white and Christian supremacy, capitalism, gender and sexual oppression, and forms of patriarchy.
  5. Leadership by affected communitiesOrganizations should be led by, or accountable to, people most affected by the structural issues they seek to address.

These criteria are important because the fund is not simply designed for any nonprofit seeking general financial assistance. Applicants should show how their organization’s work fits within Resist’s grassroots movement-building approach.

Organizations and Activities Resist Does Not Fund

The grant page lists several categories that are generally excluded from funding. These include:

  • Individuals applying in their personal capacity.
  • Social service projects.
  • Research projects.
  • Legal defense costs or lawsuits that are not directly connected to a progressive organizing campaign.
  • Material aid campaigns.
  • Projects whose primary work is outside the United States.
  • Organizations with access to traditional sources of funding.
  • Capital campaigns.
  • Capital projects.
  • Endowments.
  • Other foundations or grantmaking organizations.
  • Organizations with annual budgets of US$150,000 or more.

Applicants should carefully review these exclusions before beginning an application.

For example, an organization that provides social services may not qualify simply because its work benefits a vulnerable population. The application should demonstrate a clear connection to grassroots organizing, community power, structural change, or movement-building.

Similarly, a project that is primarily a research study may not qualify unless it is part of a broader organizing strategy that fits Resist’s priorities.

Important Note About Movement Bank Awards

The grant page states that organizations receiving Movement Bank 2026 awards are not eligible for the Urgent Action Fund or Rapid Response funding.

Applicants should therefore confirm whether their organization has received a Movement Bank award in 2026 before applying.

The Movement’s Bank Grant Cycle is a separate grantmaking stream. For 2026, the Movement Bank is described as invite-only, with decisions made by a grant panel composed of former grantees. It provides awards of approximately US$10,000, but it is not currently accepting general applications.

Application Deadline

The next Urgent Action Fund application cycle is scheduled for:

September 14–18, 2026

The stated deadline is:

September 18, 2026

The application window is part of Resist’s monthly cycle structure, under which applications open on the last Monday and close on the following Friday until the available funding cap has been reached.

Because the funding cap may be reached before the end of the stated period, applicants should submit their applications as soon as possible rather than waiting until the deadline day.

Applicants should also verify the current status on the official Resist grants page before submitting, especially if the application window has recently opened or if the fund may have reached capacity.

How to Apply for the Resist Urgent Action Fund

All applications for Resist grants must be submitted online.

The application process generally involves the following steps.

Step 1: Confirm Eligibility

Applicants should first take Resist’s online eligibility quiz. The quiz is designed to help organizations determine whether their work, organizational structure, budget, and geographic focus fit the grant requirements.

Before beginning, confirm that the organization:

  • Is based in the United States.
  • Has 501(c)(3) status or a qualifying fiscal sponsor.
  • Has an annual budget below US$150,000.
  • Is not an individual applicant.
  • Does not primarily conduct work outside the United States.
  • Is not a 2026 Movement Bank award recipient.
  • Is engaged in grassroots organizing, social justice, direct action, mutual aid, accessibility, campaigning, or related movement work.

Step 2: Access the Online Application Portal

Applicants can begin the application process through Resist’s online grant application system.

The official application portal is hosted through Grant Interface:

Resist Grant Application Portal

The official grant information page is available here:

Resist Grants Open Page

Step 3: Create a User Account

Applicants must create an account before they can browse the grant programmes, read application instructions, or submit an application.

According to Resist, creating an account should take less than five minutes. Creating an account does not require applicants to submit an application immediately.

Step 4: Review the Programme Instructions

Once logged in, applicants will see information about Resist’s grant programmes and instructions for applying.

Applicants should read the instructions carefully because the specific questions, required information, and submission procedures may vary according to the grant programme.

Step 5: Prepare and Submit the Application

The application should clearly explain:

  • The organization’s mission and work.
  • The community or communities served.
  • The urgent need or opportunity.
  • The proposed activity.
  • Why the activity requires timely funding.
  • How the activity connects to grassroots organizing or movement-building.
  • The amount requested.
  • How the funds will be used.
  • How the work is led by or accountable to affected communities.

Applicants should ensure that the information provided is accurate, specific, and consistent with the organization’s actual work.

APPLY HERE

Application Preparation Tips

1. Explain the Urgency Clearly

Because this is an Urgent Action Fund, the application should explain why the project or request requires timely support.

Avoid presenting the proposal as a general organizational wish list. Instead, describe the immediate situation, emerging opportunity, campaign development, event, direct action, accessibility need, or urgent organizing requirement.

2. Connect the Request to Broader Organizing

Resist does not fund projects solely because they are useful or beneficial. Applicants should demonstrate how the proposed activity contributes to broader social justice organizing and collective change.

Explain:

  • The movement or community context.
  • The issue being addressed.
  • The organization’s role.
  • The people involved.
  • The expected contribution to the broader campaign or organizing effort.

3. Demonstrate Community Leadership

Resist prioritizes organizations led by people most affected by structural oppression. Applicants should explain how affected communities participate in:

  • Decision-making.
  • Leadership.
  • Strategy development.
  • Campaign planning.
  • Implementation.
  • Evaluation or reflection.

4. Be Specific About the Use of Funds

Provide a clear explanation of how the grant would be used. A simple budget or cost breakdown can help reviewers understand the request.

For example, an organization might describe costs related to:

  • Accessibility services.
  • Event logistics.
  • Organizing materials.
  • Transportation connected to a campaign.
  • Venue-related costs.
  • Community mobilization.
  • Urgent communications.
  • Other eligible activities.

The proposed expenses should be directly connected to the urgent project.

5. Confirm the Organization’s Budget

Since the budget must be below US$150,000, applicants should ensure that the organization’s financial information is accurate and current.

If the organization operates under a fiscal sponsor, applicants should clarify which budget figures and organizational details the application requires.

6. Review the Exclusions

Before submitting, check that the request is not primarily for:

  • Individual support.
  • A social service project.
  • A standalone research project.
  • A capital campaign.
  • A capital project.
  • An endowment.
  • A material aid campaign.
  • Work conducted primarily outside the United States.
  • An activity that falls outside Resist’s movement-building focus.

7. Apply Early

The September 2026 application window closes on September 18, but Resist states that applications open monthly until the funding cap is reached.

Submitting early is therefore advisable. Applicants should not assume that the fund will remain open until the final day if the available resources have already been allocated.

Technical and Application Support

Resist instructs applicants to follow the online application system’s instructions for technical support.

For application-related support, applicants may contact Nicki at:

Applicants should use the support contact for questions about eligibility, application procedures, or technical difficulties that cannot be resolved through the online portal.

What Happens After Applying?

Resist indicates that it generally aims to announce Urgent Action Fund decisions approximately one month after the submission window closes. However, the timing may vary depending on the number of applications received, and there may be small delays.

Applicants should therefore monitor their email and application account after submitting.

The grant page also states that Resist distributes grants through bank transfer. Successful grantees should watch for an email from Ramp to provide payment information.

Reporting Requirements

One notable feature of Resist’s grantmaking approach is that it does not require a formal report from grantees.

Resist states that it trusts grantees to use the funds to advance their work and does not require a report. However, the organization welcomes updates from grantees who wish to share information about their organizing and community impact.

This approach is intended to reduce administrative burdens and allow organizations to focus more of their capacity on their work.

About Resist’s Grantmaking Approach

Resist describes its funding model as a form of resource redistribution rather than conventional philanthropy. The organization seeks to support grassroots movements and frontline communities that are working toward justice, liberation, and structural change.

Its grantmaking model emphasizes:

  • Grassroots leadership.
  • Community accountability.
  • Flexible funding.
  • Reduced administrative burdens.
  • Participatory decision-making.
  • Support for organizations with limited access to traditional funding.
  • Movement-building rather than isolated project delivery.

Resist’s general grant decisions are made by panels of former grantees who are paid and trained to review applications. This participatory approach is intended to place decision-making power closer to the communities and movements that receive the resources.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Resist Urgent Action Fund Grant 2026

Important Distinction: Urgent Action Fund and Movement’s Bank

Applicants should distinguish between the two grant programmes listed on the Resist page.

Urgent Action Fund

  • Status: Open during the stated application cycle.
  • Grant amount: Up to US$5,000.
  • Purpose: Urgent projects, direct actions, accessibility, mutual aid, campaigns, events, and related activities.
  • Eligibility: New and returning eligible 501(c)(3) or fiscally sponsored organizations.
  • Budget requirement: Below US$150,000.
  • Application cycle: September 14–18, 2026.

Movement’s Bank Grant Cycle

  • Status: Closed or not accepting applications.
  • Grant amount: US$10,000.
  • Purpose: Organizations with consistent, active, and emerging programming.
  • Application process: Invite-only.
  • Decision-making: Grant panel composed of former grantees.

Organizations should apply to the programme that matches their eligibility and current status. The Movement’s Bank is not a general open-call opportunity for new applicants in the 2026 information provided.

Conclusion

The Resist Urgent Action Fund Grant 2026 provides an opportunity for small, United States-based grassroots organizations to obtain up to US$5,000 for urgent organizing needs, direct actions, campaigns, accessibility initiatives, mutual aid, events, and other movement-building activities.

The fund is particularly relevant to organizations with annual budgets below US$150,000 that have 501(c)(3) status or operate under a fiscal sponsor. Applicants should demonstrate a clear connection to social justice movements, community-led organizing, structural change, and the needs of people most affected by oppression.

The next application window runs from September 14 to September 18, 2026. Eligible organizations should review the official criteria, complete the eligibility quiz, create an account on the application portal, and submit a well-prepared application before the deadline or before the available funding cap is reached.

For the latest application instructions and grant status, visit the official Resist Grants Open page and the Resist online grant application portal.

item.content:encoded:
The European Security and Defence College (ESDC) has opened applications for its 2027 internship programme, offering students the opportunity to gain practical experience within an EU institutional environment in Brussels, Belgium. The programme provides two internship periods in 2027 and is designed for students pursuing relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree programmes who want practical exposure to the European Union’s Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP) and the wider Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP).

Selected interns will receive a monthly allowance of EUR 1,500, while eligible expenses for occasional duty trips outside Brussels may also be reimbursed. Applications must be submitted by 12:00 CET on 14 October 2026.

About the European Security and Defence College Internship

The ESDC is a European Union institution focused on education and training in the area of the EU’s Common Security and Defence Policy within the broader framework of the Common Foreign and Security Policy.

According to the official 2027 internship call, the programme is intended to give students an opportunity to work directly with the ESDC and contribute to the organisation and implementation of its activities. Through this practical experience, interns can develop a stronger understanding of CSDP and CFSP while applying knowledge gained through their academic studies.

The ESDC operates as a network that brings together civilian and military institutes, universities, academies and other organisations working in the fields of security and defence. Its activities therefore provide interns with exposure to a broad institutional and international environment.

The ESDC works under the overall responsibility of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, while the European External Action Service (EEAS) supports the High Representative in carrying out responsibilities relating to the EU’s foreign and security policy.

For students interested in international relations, diplomacy, security studies, defence policy, European affairs and related disciplines, the internship provides an opportunity to gain experience in an environment directly connected to these areas.

ESDC Internship 2027 Overview

Here are the key details applicants should know:

  • Host institution: European Security and Defence College (ESDC)
  • Location: Brussels, Belgium
  • First internship period: 18 January – 14 May 2027
  • Second internship period: 29 March – 30 July 2027
  • Monthly allowance: EUR 1,500
  • Application deadline: 12:00 CET, 14 October 2026
  • Application method: Email
  • Required application documents: CV and motivation letter
  • Application language: English or French
  • CV format: European CV/Europass format
  • Target applicants: Students currently enrolled in relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree programmes
  • Citizenship requirement: Applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State
  • Working languages: English or French, with knowledge of another language considered an asset

ESDC Internship Periods for 2027

Applicants can apply for one of the two internship periods announced for 2027.

First Internship Period

The first internship will run from

18 January – 14 May 2027

Second Internship Period

The second internship will run from

29 March – 30 July 2027

Applicants are required to indicate their preferred or available internship period as part of their application.

The ESDC also indicates that a third internship period, running from 1 September to 31 December 2027, is expected to be published in March 2027. This third period is therefore not part of the current application call.

What Will ESDC Interns Do?

The internship is designed to provide practical experience rather than purely academic exposure. Successful candidates will support the ESDC Secretariat and contribute to a range of activities associated with security and defence policy training and education.

The official call identifies several responsibilities that interns may undertake.

1. Support Courses, Seminars and Conferences

Interns will assist with the preparation, implementation and post-processing of ESDC courses, seminars and conferences.

These activities may take place in Brussels or abroad and focus on CSDP and the broader CFSP framework.

This means interns can gain exposure to the planning and delivery of institutional events involving stakeholders working in European security and defence.

2. Prepare Course Materials and Background Documents

Interns may be responsible for helping prepare:

  • Course materials
  • Background briefs
  • Reports
  • Supporting documentation

This responsibility can provide useful experience in policy research, institutional writing, briefing preparation and information management.

3. Provide Meeting and Administrative Support

Interns will provide logistical and administrative assistance for meetings involving ESDC bodies, topic-focused configurations and ESDC stakeholders.

They may also:

  • Attend meetings
  • Take meeting notes
  • Help prepare meetings
  • Support post-meeting activities
  • Assist with coordination and follow-up

This aspect of the internship can be particularly relevant to students interested in diplomacy, international organisations, public administration, foreign affairs and policy coordination.

4. Support eLearning Activities

The ESDC also expects interns to support the revision of its eLearning modules.

This could expose interns to institutional digital learning content, training development and the review of educational materials.

5. Maintain the Annual Training and Course Catalogue

Interns may assist in maintaining the ESDC’s annual training and course catalogue.

This involves supporting the organisation and management of information relating to the College’s training activities.

6. Contribute to the ESDC Annual Report

Interns may also support the drafting of the ESDC Annual Report.

This can provide practical exposure to institutional reporting, information gathering, drafting and documentation.

7. Support Knowledge Management

Another important responsibility involves supporting the ESDC Secretariat’s internal Lessons Identified / Lessons Learnt and knowledge-management processes.

This component can give interns insight into how international institutions capture experience, document lessons and use organisational knowledge to improve future activities.

8. Proofread Documents and Draft Social Media Posts

The internship also includes communication-related responsibilities.

Interns may be expected to:

  • Proofread institutional documents
  • Draft social media posts
  • Support the preparation of communications content

This makes the opportunity potentially relevant not only to security and international-relations students, but also to students whose academic backgrounds combine international affairs with communications, public information, digital media or related fields, provided their programme is considered relevant to ESDC activities.

Who Can Apply for the ESDC Internship 2027?

The ESDC has established specific eligibility requirements.

Applicants must meet all applicable eligibility criteria outlined in the official call.

1. EU Citizenship Is Required

Applicants must be nationals of a Member State of the European Union.

This is an important requirement for prospective applicants from outside the European Union. The official call does not establish general eligibility for nationals of non-EU countries.

Therefore, applicants from African, Asian, American, Middle Eastern or other non-EU countries would not meet the stated nationality requirement unless they are also nationals of an EU Member State.

2. Current Bachelor’s or Master’s Students

Candidates must currently be enrolled at an academic institution or university with a view to obtaining a:

  • Bachelor’s degree;
  • Master’s degree; or
  • Equivalent qualification.

Their field of study must be relevant to the activities of the ESDC.

The internship is therefore aimed primarily at currently enrolled students, rather than applicants who have already completed their studies and are no longer enrolled.

3. Students Must Remain Enrolled Throughout the Internship

Applicants must remain enrolled at their academic institution or university for the entire duration of the internship.

This means applicants should carefully consider their expected graduation date before applying.

A student whose enrolment ends before the completion of the selected internship period may not satisfy this requirement.

4. Health and Accident Insurance

Candidates must have insurance covering sickness and accidents for the entire duration of the internship.

Applicants should therefore ensure that appropriate coverage will be available throughout their selected internship period.

5. Language Requirement

Applicants must have a thorough knowledge of at least one EU working language: English or French.

Knowledge of another language is considered an additional asset.

What Academic Backgrounds May Be Relevant?

The official call does not provide an exhaustive list of qualifying degree programmes. Instead, it requires candidates to be enrolled in a field relevant to ESDC activities.

Given the College’s mandate and the responsibilities listed in the internship call, potentially relevant academic areas may include fields connected to:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Security studies
  • Defence studies
  • European studies
  • Political science
  • Foreign policy
  • International security
  • Strategic studies
  • Peace and conflict studies
  • Public policy
  • International law
  • European affairs
  • Related social sciences and policy disciplines

Applicants should rely on the ESDC’s official assessment of whether their particular academic profile is relevant rather than assuming that a specific degree automatically qualifies.

Selection Criteria

Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not necessarily guarantee selection.

The ESDC states that applicants will be assessed based on several qualifications, including:

  1. Academic achievements
  2. Academic profile
  3. International profile
  4. Work experience

This means applicants should present their academic and professional background clearly and demonstrate how their studies and experience relate to the work of the ESDC.

Students with relevant international exposure, academic projects, internships, research activities or work experience may wish to make those aspects clear in their application where applicable.

What Does the ESDC Internship Offer?

One of the most significant features of the programme is the financial allowance.

EUR 1,500 Monthly Allowance

Selected interns will receive a monthly allowance of EUR 1,500.

The call also explains how the allowance interacts with certain external grants.

For example, if an intern receives a grant such as an Erasmus+ grant, the ESDC will reimburse the difference up to the EUR 1,500 monthly amount.

Reimbursement for Certain Duty-Trip Expenses

Interns may participate in ESDC duty trips outside Brussels, subject to budget availability.

The ESDC states that interns will be reimbursed for expenses associated with occasional duty trips outside Brussels.

This provides an additional opportunity for selected interns to gain exposure to ESDC activities beyond the institution’s Brussels base.

Internship Mentorship and Responsibilities

Interns will be placed under the responsibility of a mentor.

They are expected to follow instructions provided by their mentors and ESDC superiors and maintain high standards of:

  • Personal integrity
  • Impartiality
  • Courtesy

Interns are also required to keep a careful record of their activities and submit a report to their mentor at the end of the internship.

After completing the internship, the ESDC will provide a certificate confirming the internship.

Working Hours and Leave

Interns will work the same working hours as ESDC staff and will have the same official public holidays as ESDC employees.

They are also entitled to two working days of leave per month.

These provisions provide applicants with a clearer understanding of the institutional nature of the internship and the expectations associated with participating in the programme.

Equal Opportunities and Inclusion

The ESDC states that it is committed to an equal-opportunities policy for its staff and applicants.

The College says it is committed to:

  • Promoting gender equality;
  • Preventing discrimination on any grounds;
  • Welcoming qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds; and
  • Maintaining the broadest possible geographical representation among EU Member States.

Candidates with disabilities may request assistance or reasonable accommodation during the selection process.

The official call instructs candidates requiring accommodation to contact the ESDC vacancies address so that appropriate support can be considered.

Documents Required to Apply

Applicants must submit:

  • A CV
  • A motivation letter

The documents must be submitted in English or French and should be provided in PDF or Word format.

The ESDC specifically requests applicants to use the European CV format.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their CV clearly communicates their academic background, relevant experience, international exposure, language abilities and other information relevant to the internship.

How to Apply for the ESDC Internship 2027

Applications must be submitted by email only.

Applicants should send their application to:

esdc-vacancies@eeas.europa.eu

The application process involves screening applications against the internship requirements. The most suitable candidates may subsequently be invited to an interview by the ESDC.

Applicants must also:

  1. Indicate their availability for the internship period.
  2. Identify a point of contact or supervisor at their academic institution or university.
  3. Submit all required documents.
  4. Ensure that the application is complete.
  5. Submit the application before the specified deadline.

The ESDC explicitly states that incomplete applications will not be considered.

ESDC Internship 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline is

14 October 2026 at 12:00 CET

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their documents because applications must be complete and sent through the specified email channel.

The official ESDC webpage and internship call both confirm the 14 October 2026, 12:00 CET deadline.

APPLY HERE

Important Points Applicants Should Check Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should verify that they satisfy the core requirements.

Eligibility checklist

Applicants should confirm that they:

  • Are nationals of an EU Member State.
  • Are currently enrolled in a bachelor’s, master’s or equivalent degree programme.
  • Are studying a field relevant to ESDC activities.
  • Will remain enrolled throughout the entire internship.
  • Have sickness and accident insurance covering the entire internship.
  • Have a thorough knowledge of English or French.
  • Can provide a CV in the requested European format.
  • Can prepare a motivation letter in English or French.
  • Can identify an academic institution/university contact or supervisor.
  • Can commit to one of the announced internship periods.
  • Can submit a complete application before the deadline.

Why This Internship May Be Relevant to International Affairs Students

The ESDC internship combines academic learning with practical institutional work in an area closely connected to European and international security policy.

Interns can potentially gain experience in several areas, including:

  • International security and defence policy
  • European foreign and security policy
  • Policy-oriented research
  • Institutional coordination
  • International conferences and seminars
  • Meeting management
  • Briefing and report preparation
  • Knowledge management
  • eLearning
  • Strategic communication
  • Social media content development
  • Administrative and logistical coordination

The combination of these functions can provide a broad institutional perspective for students whose studies are connected to international affairs and related disciplines.

Visit HERE for more information about the ESDC Internship 2027 in Brussels, Belgium.

Academic qualification

Applicants must:

  • Be currently enrolled at an academic institution or university;
  • Be pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s or equivalent degree;
  • Be studying a field relevant to the ESDC’s activities; and
  • Remain enrolled for the entire duration of the internship.

Nationality and geographical eligibility

The opportunity is restricted to nationals of European Union Member States.

Therefore, nationality is a significant eligibility condition. Being a student at a European university by itself does not satisfy the stated nationality requirement.

Applicants from non-EU countries who do not also hold nationality of an EU Member State are not eligible under the nationality criterion in this particular call.

Conclusion

The ESDC Internship 2027 provides eligible students with an opportunity to gain practical experience within a European Union institutional environment focused on security and defence policy. Based in Brussels, Belgium, the programme offers two internship periods in 2027 and includes a EUR 1,500 monthly allowance.

The internship involves a broad range of activities, including supporting courses and conferences, preparing briefing materials and reports, assisting with meetings, contributing to eLearning and knowledge-management activities, supporting the annual report and drafting social media content.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to students whose academic studies connect with international relations, security and defence, European affairs, diplomacy, foreign policy, public policy and related areas. However, applicants must carefully note the nationality requirement: candidates must be nationals of an EU Member State, must remain enrolled in their academic programme throughout the internship and must satisfy the language, insurance and other eligibility requirements.

Applications must include a CV and motivation letter in English or French and must be submitted by email to the ESDC vacancies address. The final deadline is 12:00 CET on 14 October 2026.

For more Internship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The LawAI Seasonal Fellowships provide an opportunity for law students, legal professionals, researchers, academics, and other qualified specialists to engage with some of the most important emerging questions at the intersection of artificial intelligence, law, regulation, and public policy.

As artificial intelligence continues to develop rapidly, governments, regulators, courts, researchers, technology organizations, and policymakers are increasingly confronted with complex questions about how advanced AI systems should be governed. LawAI’s Seasonal Fellowships are designed to bring researchers and practitioners into this evolving field, allowing fellows to contribute to research while interacting with people working on frontier AI policy.

The fellowship opportunities are particularly relevant to individuals interested in AI governance, technology regulation, public policy, legal research, emerging technologies, and the development of legal frameworks for increasingly capable AI systems.

LawAI encourages prospective applicants to review its workstreams and research directions before applying so that they can understand the organization’s areas of interest and identify how their own research experience, legal background, and professional interests could contribute.

What Are the LawAI Seasonal Fellowships?

LawAI’s Seasonal Fellowships are structured research opportunities for individuals who want to work at the leading edge of AI, law, and policy.

The program currently includes three principal fellowship tracks:

  1. Winter Research Fellowship (EU Law)
  2. Summer Fellowship (US)
  3. Summer Research Fellowship (Legal Frontiers)

Each track has a somewhat different geographic and substantive focus. While the US and EU Law tracks place particular emphasis on legal experience in their respective jurisdictions, the Legal Frontiers fellowship provides a broader interdisciplinary pathway for researchers whose work can contribute to the development of law and public policy surrounding advanced AI.

Applicants may apply to multiple tracks where they meet the relevant qualifications. However, a separate application must be submitted for each fellowship track.

1. Winter Research Fellowship in EU Law

The Winter Research Fellowship focuses on legal and policy questions connected to the European Union.

This fellowship is particularly relevant to candidates who have studied or worked with EU law and who are interested in applying their legal research capabilities to questions arising from artificial intelligence and emerging technology regulation.

LawAI strongly encourages fellows in this track to participate in person in Cambridge, United Kingdom. According to LawAI, a significant part of the value of the fellowship comes from developing professional connections with other fellows and interacting directly with LawAI staff and individuals working on frontier AI policy who visit the Cambridge office.

The organization recognizes, however, that circumstances differ between applicants. Remote participation may therefore be considered on a case-by-case basis where a candidate has compelling reasons, such as family commitments.

Convening Week

The Winter Research Fellowship includes an in-person Convening Week in Cambridge, UK, scheduled for:

February 8–12

Applicants considering this track should therefore be prepared to meet any relevant travel, immigration, and participation requirements associated with attending the Convening Week.

Fellowship Subsidy

Fellows participating in the Winter Research Fellowship receive:

  • £1,000 per week fellowship subsidy.
  • A one-off £7,000 relocation and housing payment for fellows who relocate to Cambridge.

Candidates with exceptional experience or qualifications may be eligible for higher subsidies.

2. Summer Fellowship in the United States

The Summer Fellowship is focused on US law and policy and is designed for candidates with relevant legal study or professional experience in the United States.

The fellowship is particularly suitable for individuals interested in the relationship between artificial intelligence and US legal and policy frameworks.

LawAI strongly encourages fellows to participate in person in Washington, DC. The organization notes that being embedded within the team and the wider Washington policy community can provide significant opportunities for professional interaction, research collaboration, and engagement with the broader AI policy environment.

Remote arrangements may nevertheless be considered on a case-by-case basis for candidates with compelling reasons to participate remotely.

Convening Week

The Summer Fellowship includes an in-person Convening Week in Washington, DC, scheduled for:

June 21–25

Candidates should take this requirement into account when determining whether the fellowship’s participation arrangements are compatible with their circumstances.

Fellowship Subsidy

The Summer Fellowship provides:

  • $2,000 per week subsidy.
  • A $10,000 relocation and housing stipend for fellows who relocate to Washington, DC.

The relocation and housing stipend is treated as taxable income. LawAI states that recipients are not required to submit reimbursement claims or receipts for this stipend.

As with the other tracks, candidates with exceptional experience or qualifications may be eligible for higher subsidies.

3. Summer Research Fellowship in Legal Frontiers

The Summer Research Fellowship in Legal Frontiers provides a broader research pathway for candidates interested in the future of law and public policy in the context of advanced AI.

Unlike the US and EU Law tracks, this fellowship does not require applicants to have a primary background in law. LawAI specifically welcomes applicants from other disciplines where their research can contribute meaningfully to questions involving advanced AI governance.

Potentially relevant backgrounds include:

  • Computer science
  • Public policy
  • Economics
  • History
  • Psychology
  • Physics
  • Law
  • Other disciplines relevant to the development of law and public policy

Applicants without specialized knowledge of US, EU, or UK law may still be considered, although LawAI indicates that candidates without expertise in one of these jurisdictions are generally considered only in exceptional circumstances.

Remote-First Structure

The Legal Frontiers fellowship is designed as a remote-first opportunity.

Fellows may have opportunities for in-person participation at LawAI’s Cambridge office in the United Kingdom or with the organization’s US Law & Policy team in Washington, DC.

Previous Summer Research Fellows have found value in being embedded within the organization and participating in the wider research and policy communities.

Convening Week

The Legal Frontiers fellowship’s Convening Week is hosted in Washington, DC:

June 21–25

Applicants should therefore consider the in-person Convening Week requirement when assessing their ability to participate.

Fellowship Subsidy

The Legal Frontiers fellowship provides a weekly subsidy based on the fellow’s location. LawAI gives the following examples:

  • $1,800 per week for Summer Research Fellows based in the United States.
  • £1,000 per week for fellows based in the European Union and United Kingdom.
  • Additional stipends may potentially be available when location-specific conditions are met.

Candidates with exceptional qualifications or experience may also be eligible for higher subsidies.

Who Can Apply for LawAI Seasonal Fellowships?

LawAI’s Seasonal Fellowships are intended for applicants with meaningful legal, policy, research, or academic experience relevant to the fellowship track they select.

The organization explicitly states that it welcomes applications from professionals, meaning the opportunities are not restricted exclusively to current students.

Potential applicants include:

  • Law students
  • Practicing lawyers
  • Legal researchers
  • Law and policy researchers
  • Academics
  • Public policy researchers
  • Researchers from relevant interdisciplinary fields
  • Professionals with experience relevant to AI law and policy

The precise requirements depend on the fellowship track.

Requirements for the US and EU Law Tracks

For the US and EU Law tracks, LawAI generally expects applicants to have formal legal training or experience.

This is important because these fellowships require candidates to understand the legal principles applicable to AI regulation within the relevant jurisdiction.

Applicants should therefore have some form of formal legal education, professional legal experience, or another substantive background that demonstrates their understanding of the applicable legal system.

For the US track, relevant experience with US law is expected.

For the EU Law track, relevant experience with EU law is expected.

LawAI also encourages applications from people who previously studied or practiced US or EU law but are currently living and working in another country.

Requirements for the Legal Frontiers Track

The Legal Frontiers fellowship has a broader eligibility approach.

Applicants do not necessarily need to have law as their primary academic or professional discipline. Instead, candidates should be able to clearly demonstrate how their research could positively contribute to the development of law and public policy relating to advanced artificial intelligence.

This makes the fellowship potentially relevant to researchers working across multiple disciplines.

For example, a computer scientist might explore technical developments that have implications for AI governance. An economist might investigate regulatory incentives or the economic effects of AI policy. A historian might contribute research into institutional development and technology governance, while a psychologist could examine human behavior and policy implications associated with increasingly capable AI systems.

Candidates who intend to conduct technical research during the fellowship are responsible for identifying and securing an appropriately qualified technical supervisor.

Is Previous AI Experience Required?

Previous specialized experience with AI-related legal questions is not required.

Applicants should nevertheless have an interest in artificial intelligence, law, and policy and should be prepared to apply their research skills and existing knowledge to questions in the field.

This means applicants do not necessarily need to have already established a career specializing in AI law.

Instead, candidates can demonstrate their suitability through:

  • Strong research capabilities
  • Relevant legal or policy knowledge
  • Academic or professional experience
  • Interest in AI governance
  • Ability to investigate complex emerging questions
  • Ability to connect their existing expertise with AI-related legal and policy issues

The absence of a requirement for previous AI-specific experience potentially makes these fellowships accessible to qualified researchers who are transitioning into the field.

English Language Requirement

Applicants are required to have full professional fluency in English, both spoken and written.

This requirement reflects the collaborative nature of the fellowships. Fellows are expected to actively participate in:

  • Research discussions
  • Professional collaborations
  • Presentations
  • Meetings
  • Academic and policy conversations
  • Other activities requiring effective written and spoken communication

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating complex legal, policy, or research ideas in English.

Are Practicing Professionals Eligible?

Yes.

LawAI explicitly welcomes professionals, including practicing lawyers, law and policy researchers, and academics.

Relevant professional experience is highly valued, making these fellowships potentially suitable for candidates who are already working in legal practice, research, academia, regulation, public policy, or related areas.

The opportunities can therefore be relevant to both emerging researchers and established professionals seeking to deepen their involvement in AI law and policy.

Are the LawAI Seasonal Fellowships Paid?

Yes. LawAI provides weekly subsidies to fellows, with the exact amount depending on the fellowship track and the fellow’s location.

The stated financial support includes:

Winter Research Fellowship (EU Law)

  • £1,000 per week
  • One-off £7,000 relocation and housing payment for fellows relocating to Cambridge

APPLY HERE

Summer Fellowship (US)

  • $2,000 per week
  • $10,000 relocation and housing stipend for fellows relocating to Washington, DC

The US relocation and housing stipend is treated as taxable income, and LawAI states that recipients do not need to provide receipts or reimbursement documentation.

APPLY HERE

Summer Research Fellowship (Legal Frontiers)

  • $1,800 per week for fellows based in the US
  • £1,000 per week for fellows based in the EU and UK
  • Potential additional location-specific stipends

LawAI also indicates that candidates with exceptional experience or qualifications may be eligible for higher subsidies.

Applicants should carefully review the applicable fellowship description for the specific track they intend to pursue because payment arrangements may vary according to location and individual circumstances.

APPLY HERE

Remote and In-Person Participation

The Seasonal Fellowships do not all follow the same participation model.

A common feature across the program is the requirement for an in-person Convening Week.

Outside of that period, participation varies according to the fellowship.

Winter Research Fellowship

The Winter Research Fellowship strongly encourages in-person participation in Cambridge. Remote participation may be considered in exceptional circumstances.

The Convening Week takes place in Cambridge from February 8–12.

Summer Fellowship

The US Summer Fellowship strongly encourages in-person participation in Washington, DC. Remote participation may be considered on a case-by-case basis for candidates with compelling reasons.

The Convening Week takes place in Washington, DC, from June 21–25.

Legal Frontiers Fellowship

The Legal Frontiers fellowship is remote-first.

Nevertheless, fellows may have opportunities to participate in person from Cambridge or Washington, DC, and the Convening Week is hosted in Washington, DC, from June 21–25.

Applicants should therefore distinguish between a fellowship being remote-first or allowing remote arrangements and the separate requirement to participate in an in-person Convening Week.

Visa and Immigration Requirements

Successful applicants are responsible for having any visa or immigration authorization required to participate in the fellowship in the relevant country.

LawAI states that, after making an offer, it will make every reasonable effort to support relevant visa applications where appropriate.

However, visa eligibility is ultimately determined by the relevant immigration authorities.

Applicants who would need to travel internationally for a fellowship should therefore investigate applicable immigration requirements early in the application process.

Can Applicants Apply for More Than One Fellowship Track?

Yes.

Applicants may apply for multiple Seasonal Fellowship tracks, including:

  • US
  • EU Law
  • Legal Frontiers

However, applicants must meet the relevant qualifications for each track they select.

A separate application must also be submitted for each fellowship.

Candidates considering multiple tracks should therefore ensure that each application is appropriately tailored to the specific jurisdiction, research focus, and requirements of that fellowship rather than submitting identical materials without modification.

What Makes the Seasonal Fellowships Relevant to AI Governance?

The rapid development of artificial intelligence is creating new questions for legal systems and policymakers.

Issues surrounding advanced AI can involve regulation, liability, governance, public policy, institutional design, technological development, economic impacts, and the relationship between emerging technologies and existing legal frameworks.

LawAI’s Seasonal Fellowships provide a structured environment for researchers to investigate these types of questions while engaging with other people working in the field.

The opportunity is therefore not simply about studying AI as a technology. It is about examining how law and public policy may respond to increasingly capable AI systems.

For applicants with backgrounds in law, public policy, economics, computer science, history, psychology, physics, or related disciplines, this interdisciplinary environment can provide a setting in which existing research expertise can be applied to emerging questions surrounding advanced AI.

How Applicants Can Prepare

Prospective applicants should begin by understanding the research areas relevant to LawAI and the particular fellowship track they intend to apply for.

Useful preparation steps include:

  1. Review LawAI’s research directions.
    Applicants should familiarize themselves with the organization’s workstreams and research priorities.
  2. Identify the most suitable fellowship track.
    Candidates should consider whether their background aligns most closely with US law, EU law, or the broader Legal Frontiers research agenda.
  3. Connect previous experience to AI law and policy.
    Even though previous AI-specific experience is not mandatory, applicants should be able to explain why their existing knowledge and research abilities are relevant to AI-related questions.
  4. Demonstrate strong research ability.
    Applications should clearly communicate the candidate’s ability to investigate complex questions, analyze evidence, and develop meaningful research.
  5. Consider the geographic requirements.
    Candidates should review the in-person Convening Week dates and determine whether they can meet the relevant participation requirements.
  6. Review visa requirements if international travel is necessary.
    Applicants who may need immigration authorization should consider the relevant requirements well in advance.
  7. Prepare for professional collaboration in English.
    Since full professional English fluency is required, candidates should be prepared to participate confidently in discussions, collaborations, and presentations.

Can Applicants Receive Individualized Feedback?

LawAI states that it cannot provide personalized feedback to applicants.

The organization carefully reviews applications but receives a high volume of submissions, making individualized feedback impractical.

Applicants should therefore aim to submit complete, carefully prepared applications that clearly demonstrate their qualifications, research interests, and suitability for the particular fellowship track.

How to Stay Updated About Future LawAI Fellowships

Applicants who are interested in future fellowship opportunities can stay connected with LawAI through its communication channels.

LawAI encourages prospective applicants to follow its updates through its newsletter, LinkedIn, and X.

These channels can provide information about upcoming fellowship opportunities, events, research activities, and other ways to engage with the organization.

Long-Term Opportunities at LawAI

The Seasonal Fellowships are not the only opportunities available through LawAI.

The organization also offers longer-term roles through its open positions.

Seasonal Fellowships can provide an avenue for individuals to become involved with LawAI’s work and may serve as a stepping stone toward future full-time opportunities, although participation in a fellowship does not guarantee employment.

Candidates interested in building a longer-term career in AI law and policy should therefore also monitor LawAI’s open positions in addition to its seasonal fellowship announcements.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should carefully consider several factors.

First, applicants should select a track that corresponds with their academic, professional, and research background. The US and EU Law tracks require a stronger jurisdiction-specific legal foundation, while the Legal Frontiers track accommodates a broader range of disciplines.

Second, applicants should be prepared for the English-language requirements and the collaborative nature of the program.

Third, candidates should consider whether they can participate in the required in-person Convening Week.

Fourth, international applicants should investigate visa and immigration requirements if their selected fellowship involves participation in another country.

Finally, candidates should carefully review the full description for their selected fellowship before applying because specific details can differ between the US, EU Law, and Legal Frontiers tracks.

For

Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the information provided for the Seasonal Fellowships page.

Applicants should therefore check the individual fellowship descriptions and LawAI’s official opportunity updates for the current application period and any applicable deadline before submitting an application.

Visit HERE to learn more about the LawAI Seasonal Fellowships.

Conclusion

The LawAI Seasonal Fellowships provide research opportunities for individuals interested in the rapidly developing intersection of artificial intelligence, law, regulation, and public policy. With separate pathways focused on EU law, US law, and broader legal frontiers, the program accommodates applicants with different professional, academic, and disciplinary backgrounds.

The Winter Research Fellowship offers a European-focused opportunity with an emphasis on participation in Cambridge, while the Summer Fellowship in the United States focuses on US law and policy and encourages fellows to engage with the Washington, DC policy environment. The Summer Research Fellowship in Legal Frontiers provides a broader, remote-first pathway for researchers whose work can contribute to the development of law and public policy surrounding advanced AI.

Law students, lawyers, legal researchers, academics, policymakers, and researchers from relevant interdisciplinary fields may find the fellowships particularly relevant to their professional and research interests. Importantly, applicants do not need previous specialized experience in AI law, provided they have appropriate research or legal knowledge and a genuine interest in applying their expertise to AI-related questions.

With weekly financial subsidies, potential relocation and housing support, opportunities for professional collaboration, and exposure to researchers and practitioners working on frontier AI policy, the Seasonal Fellowships offer a structured way for qualified candidates to deepen their engagement with one of the most rapidly evolving areas of contemporary law and policy.

Prospective applicants should carefully review the specific requirements of each fellowship track, assess their jurisdictional or interdisciplinary background, prepare a strong research-focused application, and monitor LawAI’s official channels for current application deadlines and future fellowship announcements.

item.content:encoded:
The South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) is offering Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)-funded PhD studentships for September 2027 entry, providing opportunities for talented researchers in the social sciences to undertake doctoral study at one of six participating universities in London and South East England.

The studentships are open to UK and international students and include UK tuition fees and a stipend at the UKRI rate. For successful overseas applicants, the SEDarc institutions will cover the difference between UK home and international tuition fees, except for the University of Reading.

The SEDarc deadline is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT, although applicants must first complete the institutional application process, and each participating university has its own deadline and procedure.

Participating Universities

Students can be based at one of six higher education institutions:

  • University of Kent
  • Kingston University
  • University of Reading
  • Royal Holloway, University of London
  • University of Surrey
  • University of Sussex

SEDarc also works with non-higher-education partner organisations to strengthen the research and training opportunities available to doctoral students.

SEDarc Research Pathways

SEDarc’s doctoral training model combines advanced research skills training, placements and an individual research project within one of five interdisciplinary, challenge-led pathways:

  1. Living Sustainably
  2. Healthy Thriving Communities
  3. Inclusive Economic Growth
  4. Secure, Effective, & Trusted Institutions
  5. Transformative Technologies for Society

These pathways provide a framework for research addressing major social, economic, environmental, institutional and technological challenges.

Funding and Benefits

The standard SEDarc PhD lasts 3.5 years full-time, including a three-month placement, or the part-time equivalent.

The funding package covers:

  • UK tuition fees
  • A UKRI-rate stipend
  • Three-month placement
  • Research and skills training
  • Individual doctoral research
  • For eligible students without a relevant social-science Master’s degree, potential funding for an approved Master’s course within the SEDarc consortium

The UKRI has not yet announced the 2027/28 tuition fee and stipend rates.

For reference, the 2026/27 rates were:

  • UK tuition fees: £5,238
  • UKRI stipend: £21,805
  • London-weighted stipend: £23,805 where applicable

The 2027/28 figures may therefore differ.

Funding for International Students

SEDarc accepts international applications.

For successful overseas applicants, the SEDarc institutions will cover the difference between UK home tuition fees and international tuition fees.

However, an important exception applies: the University of Reading does not cover this difference.

International applicants should therefore carefully check the financial arrangements of their chosen institution before applying.

Ring-Fenced Scholarships

SEDarc is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion throughout the doctoral journey.

The programme states that it will reserve up to three ring-fenced scholarships for eligible home students from certain Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic groups.

Applicants interested in these ring-fenced studentships should review the specific eligibility criteria published by SEDarc.

Who Can Apply?

The SEDarc PhD studentships are open to:

  • UK students
  • International students
  • Applicants working across the social sciences
  • Prospective PhD researchers who meet the academic requirements of their chosen institution and programme

Applicants who do not already hold a Master’s degree in the social sciences may also be eligible for funding to undertake an approved Master’s course within the SEDarc consortium.

Eligibility for this additional Master’s funding depends on the relevant requirements.

How to Apply

Applicants cannot apply directly to SEDarc without institutional nomination.

Students must first be nominated by one of the six SEDarc universities.

The application process therefore involves:

  1. Choose one of the six participating SEDarc institutions.
  2. Identify a suitable doctoral research area and SEDarc pathway.
  3. Contact the SEDarc administrator at your chosen university.
  4. Follow that institution’s application process and deadline.
  5. Complete the institutional stage of the application.
  6. Obtain nomination from the university.
  7. Submit the SEDarc studentship application by the SEDarc deadline.

Because the six universities have different institutional deadlines and procedures, applicants should contact their chosen university as early as possible.

University Contacts

Kingston University: hssce-research@kingston.ac.uk

Royal Holloway, University of London: esrcdtp@rhul.ac.uk

University of Kent: kentgrc@kent.ac.uk

University of Reading: doctoralstudentshipsofficer@reading.ac.uk

University of Surrey: doctoralcollege@surrey.ac.uk

University of Sussex: pgr-scholarships@sussex.ac.uk

Application Deadline

The SEDarc studentship application deadline is:

29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT

Applicants should note that this is the SEDarc deadline. The university they choose will have its own earlier institutional deadline and application process.

Applicants should therefore not wait until January 2027 before contacting their chosen institution.

Important Funding Notice

SEDarc’s ESRC Doctoral Training Partnership is subject to a mid-term review in 2026.

According to the programme information, the number of studentships may be revised depending on the findings of the review.

Allocations for the 2027 cohort are expected to be confirmed around January 2027.

Conclusion

The SEDarc ESRC PhD studentships provide funded doctoral study opportunities for UK and international researchers in the social sciences, with placements, research training and interdisciplinary research pathways forming part of the programme.

Students can apply through one of six participating universities: Kent, Kingston, Reading, Royal Holloway, Surrey or Sussex.

The standard PhD is 3.5 years full-time and includes a three-month placement. Funding covers UK tuition fees and provides a UKRI-rate stipend, while arrangements for international tuition fees vary by institution.

The main SEDarc application deadline is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT, but applicants must first meet the separate institutional deadline and nomination requirements of their selected university.

Discover more on the OFY Webpage.
