item.content:encoded:
Partners for Public Good (PPG) is accepting applications for its 2026 Research Fellowship, a six-month, project-based opportunity for early-career researchers interested in improving government effectiveness through rigorous, policy-relevant research.

The fellowship is designed for researchers who want to contribute directly to research on public procurement, local government operations, technology, regulatory systems, infrastructure and government capacity.

Selected fellows will work remotely from within the United States for approximately 15 to 25 hours per week and will receive compensation of $50 per hour, with benefits as required by applicable state or local law.

The fellowship is expected to begin in October 2026, and applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The final application deadline is September 28, 2026, at close of business.

About the PPG Research Fellowship

The PPG Research Fellowship is a six-month programme that provides early-career researchers with dedicated time, mentorship and practical experience conducting research connected to government effectiveness.

Fellows will work on one of five predetermined high-priority research topics related to public procurement and local government operations.

Throughout the fellowship, participants will conduct policy-relevant background research, apply rigorous research methods to collect and analyse data, and collaborate with PPG staff and other fellows.

The programme is designed not only to generate useful research for governments but also to help fellows develop their own research portfolios through publications, policy briefs, datasets and other professional outputs.

About Partners for Public Good

Partners for Public Good (PPG) is a nonpartisan organisation that works alongside state and local governments to strengthen the operational systems that determine whether policies translate into results for residents.

Its work covers areas including:

  • Procurement
  • Staffing
  • Budgeting
  • Technology
  • Government operations
  • Applied research
  • Implementation

Rather than simply providing recommendations, PPG works directly with government staff during implementation and remains engaged until meaningful changes have been achieved.

Through its implementation work, applied research and Procurement Excellence Network, PPG shares knowledge and tools that can be applied across different jurisdictions.

The organisation’s Procurement Excellence Network includes more than 3,000 government professionals.

Why the Fellowship Focuses on Local Government

Local governments play a critical role in translating public policy into services and outcomes that residents experience every day.

Areas such as transportation, infrastructure, emergency services and school food depend on effective local government systems and operations.

However, there remains a need for more rigorous research examining how local governments manage procurement, budgeting, technology and staffing capacity, as well as how these operations are influenced by state and federal policies and regulations.

The PPG Research Fellowship aims to support a new generation of researchers who are interested in using evidence and research to improve government effectiveness.

The programme provides fellows with an opportunity to investigate practical government challenges while producing research that can contribute to broader discussions about public-sector reform.

Fellowship Structure

The fellowship lasts for six months.

Fellows will work on a defined research project under the guidance of PPG staff and alongside two other fellows.

The programme combines independent research with collaboration and professional development.

Participants will take part in activities such as:

  • Coaching calls
  • Research team meetings
  • Collaborative research activities
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Research discussions with PPG staff

Fellows will also receive support in translating their research into public-facing outputs, including draft publications and policy briefs.

Before the fellowship begins, PPG and each selected fellow will agree on:

  • Work hours
  • Project goals
  • Expected deliverables
  • Data access
  • Data use
  • Data rights
  • Data ownership

The work schedule is flexible within the agreed 15–25-hour-per-week commitment.

Five Research Topics

Applicants can express interest in one or two of the five research projects available through the fellowship.

1. Understanding Public Procurement Through Municipal Data

Public procurement is an important mechanism through which governments use public resources to provide services, infrastructure and other outcomes for residents.

However, procurement practices, systems and publicly available information can differ significantly from one jurisdiction to another.

This research project will examine publicly available information about local government procurement to develop a better understanding of procurement practices across U.S. cities.

The fellow will contribute to research designed to strengthen understanding of how governments purchase goods and services while identifying opportunities for further research and analysis.

2. The Compliance Web: Layered Governance and Local Implementation

Local governments operate within a complex system of federal, state and local laws, regulations, funding requirements and administrative procedures.

While these requirements can establish important protections and standards, they can also create administrative burdens, uncertainty and challenges for effective implementation.

This project will focus on one area, such as permitting, transit infrastructure or school food procurement, to examine how the complex “compliance web” affects local government operations and project delivery.

The research will explore where federal and state policies support or constrain local implementation and how policy design could better support effective government delivery.

3. Emerging Technology and Government Operations

State and local governments are increasingly exploring artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to support internal operations and their workforce.

These technologies may also provide new ways to understand how public servants interact with government systems and processes.

This research project will explore what the use of AI and emerging technologies can reveal about government operations, organisational capacity and opportunities for improvement.

The fellow will contribute to developing and testing new approaches to studying how government work is performed.

4. Innovative Approaches to Public Purchasing

Governments have multiple tools and approaches available for purchasing goods and services.

Different purchasing approaches can involve different advantages, limitations and trade-offs.

This project will examine emerging procurement trends, with particular attention to cooperative purchasing.

The research will explore how and why different approaches are being used across jurisdictions and consider their implications for:

  • Government efficiency
  • Market participation
  • Public procurement systems
  • The broader procurement ecosystem

5. Building Local Capacity for Stormwater Management

Communities across the United States are exploring different ways to improve their ability to manage stormwater and respond to infrastructure and resilience needs.

Approaches vary depending on local circumstances, governance structures and state and federal policy environments.

This research project will examine how communities develop and finance stormwater management capacity.

Fellows will identify patterns across jurisdictions and generate insights that can inform future research and practical approaches to stormwater management.

Fellowship Deliverables

Each fellow will be expected to complete approximately two to three deliverables during the fellowship.

Depending on the research project, deliverables may include:

  • A topic-specific literature review
  • A dataset compiled from publicly available information and supporting documentation
  • A dataset developed through primary data collection
  • Survey or interview instruments
  • A draft research publication
  • A policy brief
  • A conference submission

These outputs can provide fellows with practical research experience while strengthening their professional and academic portfolios.

Fellowship Location and Working Hours

The fellowship is a remote opportunity.

The position can be undertaken from a flexible location within the United States, but fellows must have access to a major U.S. airport because the programme includes an in-person research retreat.

Fellows will work between 15 and 25 hours per week.

The exact working hours will be agreed upon between PPG and each selected fellow before the fellowship begins.

Fellowship Compensation

Selected fellows will be compensated at a rate of:

$50 per hour

The fellowship requires approximately 15–25 hours of work per week.

Benefits will be provided where required by applicable state or local law.

The compensation structure provides fellows with paid research experience while allowing them to maintain other academic or professional commitments within the requirements of the programme.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is intended for early-career researchers and professionals with relevant research or policy experience.

Potential applicants may include:

  • Graduate students
  • Postdoctoral researchers
  • Early-career faculty
  • Research staff
  • Policy staff
  • Researchers affiliated with universities
  • Researchers affiliated with think tanks
  • Researchers affiliated with nonprofits
  • Professionals with comparable research or policy experience

Applicants may maintain an affiliation with a university, think tank, nonprofit or other research or policy organisation during the fellowship, provided they can meet the required time commitments and deliverables.

Applicants who do not have an institutional affiliation are also welcome to apply.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit the following materials:

1. Resume or CV

Applicants must submit a resume or curriculum vitae of no more than two pages.

The document should clearly present the applicant’s relevant academic, research, professional and policy experience.

2. Letter of Interest

Applicants must submit a letter of interest addressing specific questions.

The letter should explain:

  • Which one or two research projects the applicant is interested in and why.
  • Why the applicant is qualified to undertake the selected project.
  • How the applicant would approach the proposed research.

Applicants interested in two projects may submit a letter of up to three pages and should clearly identify their first-choice project.

Applicants interested in only one project should follow the two-page limit.

3. Work Sample

Applicants must provide a work sample demonstrating their research skills and expertise.

The work sample may be:

  • A published research publication
  • A research publication under review
  • Another relevant research product

Applicants should select a work sample that provides strong evidence of their ability to conduct and communicate rigorous research.

Application Deadline

The final deadline to apply for the PPG Research Fellowship is:

September 28, 2026

PPG will review applications on a rolling basis.

All applications received by the close of business on September 28, 2026 will be considered.

Applicants are encouraged to submit their materials as early as possible because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Expected Start Date

The desired start date for the fellowship is:

October 2026

Selected fellows will work with PPG before the start of the programme to establish expectations regarding working hours, research goals, deliverables and data-related matters.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Partners for Public Good is an equal opportunity employer.

The organisation states that all qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

PPG is also committed to including qualified individuals with disabilities in its hiring process.

Applicants who require reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or interview process can contact the organisation through the contact information provided in the original application announcement.

How to Apply for the PPG Research Fellowship

Interested applicants should prepare all required materials before submitting their application.

The application process includes:

  1. Review the five available research topics.
  2. Select the one or two projects that best match your interests and experience.
  3. Identify your first-choice project if applying for two.
  4. Prepare a resume or CV of no more than two pages.
  5. Prepare the required letter of interest.
  6. Select an appropriate research work sample.
  7. Review all application requirements carefully.
  8. Submit the complete application before the September 28, 2026 deadline.

Conclusion

The PPG Research Fellowship 2026 offers early-career researchers an opportunity to gain practical experience conducting policy-relevant research focused on government effectiveness and local government operations.

Over six months, fellows will work alongside PPG staff and other researchers on one of five research topics covering public procurement, regulatory compliance, emerging technology, public purchasing and stormwater management.

The programme combines independent research, collaboration, mentorship and professional development, while giving participants opportunities to produce literature reviews, datasets, publications, policy briefs and conference submissions.

Selected fellows will work remotely for 15–25 hours per week and receive $50 per hour, with benefits as required by applicable law. The fellowship is expected to begin in October 2026.

Researchers interested in contributing to evidence-based improvements in government operations should consider preparing their application early. The final deadline is September 28, 2026.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) at Pennsylvania State University has opened applications for its Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) graduate programme. The programme provides an opportunity for students interested in advanced graduate study in the behavioral sciences, human development and family studies.

Applicants interested in joining the programme must apply through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal and select the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree.

The application deadline is December 1.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to carefully review the programme requirements and prepare all required documents before submitting their applications. Applicants outside the United States should also take the application deadline and Penn State’s Eastern Standard Time zone into account when submitting their applications.

About the Penn State HDFS Graduate Programme

The Human Development and Family Studies graduate programme is designed for students pursuing advanced academic and research training in areas related to human development, family studies and the behavioral sciences.

The programme follows a doctoral pathway. HDFS does not offer a terminal master’s programme.

Students who enter the programme with a bachelor’s degree are required to complete a master’s degree en route to the doctoral degree.

Applicants should therefore select the Ph.D. degree when completing the graduate application rather than applying for a standalone master’s programme.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Penn State HDFS graduate programme is:

December 1

Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their applications are submitted by the deadline.

Penn State is located in the Eastern Standard Time zone. Applicants submitting their applications from outside the United States should account for the time difference when determining when to submit their applications.

It is recommended that applicants avoid waiting until the final hours of the deadline to submit their materials.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal.

University policy allows an applicant to apply to only one graduate degree programme at a time. Applicants interested in HDFS should therefore ensure that they select the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree when completing the application.

The application process will guide applicants through the general requirements established by the Graduate School as well as the programme-specific materials required by HDFS.

Applicants should review all requirements carefully before submitting their application.

Required Application Materials

Applicants to the HDFS graduate programme are expected to provide several documents as part of their application.

The required programme-specific materials include:

1. Scientific Writing Sample

Applicants are required to submit a scientific writing sample as part of the application.

The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to communicate academic or research-related ideas effectively and provide evidence of their writing and analytical abilities.

2. Official Transcripts

Applicants must provide official academic transcripts as required by the university.

Transcripts allow the admissions committee to assess an applicant’s previous academic preparation and educational background.

Applicants should ensure that their academic records meet Penn State Graduate School requirements.

3. Curriculum Vitae or Résumé

Applicants must submit a curriculum vitae (CV) or résumé outlining their academic, professional, research and other relevant experiences.

Applicants should ensure that the document clearly presents experiences that are relevant to their intended graduate study.

4. Statement of Professional and Career Plans

Applicants are required to submit a statement describing their professional and career plans.

This statement provides an opportunity for applicants to explain their academic and professional objectives and how doctoral study relates to their long-term goals.

Applicants should use the statement to clearly communicate their motivation for pursuing graduate education and their intended career direction.

5. Three Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation.

Recommendation letters are an important part of the application because they can provide the admissions committee with additional insight into an applicant’s academic preparation, capabilities and potential for success in graduate study.

Applicants should select recommenders who are familiar with their academic, research or professional abilities.

Applicants from Outside the United States

International applicants may have additional requirements as part of the Penn State Graduate School admissions process.

Applicants from outside the United States should carefully review the university’s requirements for international applicants and ensure that all required documentation is provided.

International applicants should also pay particular attention to application deadlines and time-zone differences when submitting their applications.

GRE Scores Are Not Required

The HDFS graduate programme does not require GRE scores as part of the application.

The department uses a holistic review process to evaluate each applicant’s potential to succeed in the programme. Applicants will receive full consideration regardless of whether they submit GRE scores.

Although GRE scores are not required, some applicants may choose to submit them if they believe the scores would provide additional evidence of their potential for graduate study in the behavioral sciences.

For example, submitting GRE scores may be useful for applicants whose undergraduate major is not closely related to the HDFS graduate curriculum or applicants returning to graduate school after working in another field.

In such circumstances, an applicant’s academic transcripts and recommendation letters may not fully demonstrate their preparation for graduate study in the behavioral sciences. Applicants may therefore consider whether additional materials, including GRE scores, would strengthen their application.

Holistic Application Review

The HDFS programme evaluates applications using a holistic review process.

This means applicants are considered based on the overall strength and potential demonstrated through their application rather than solely on one component such as standardized test scores.

Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a complete application that accurately communicates their academic preparation, research interests, experiences, professional objectives and potential for success in graduate study.

Who Should Apply?

The programme may be suitable for students and professionals interested in pursuing advanced academic and research training related to human development, family studies and the behavioral sciences.

Applicants should carefully assess their academic background and professional objectives against the HDFS programme before applying.

Students entering with a bachelor’s degree should be prepared to complete a master’s degree en route to the Ph.D.

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before submitting an application, prospective students should keep the following points in mind:

  1. The application deadline is December 1.
  2. Applications must be submitted through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal.
  3. Applicants may apply to only one graduate degree programme at a time under university policy.
  4. HDFS applicants should select the Ph.D. degree.
  5. HDFS does not offer a terminal master’s programme.
  6. Students entering with a bachelor’s degree are required to complete a master’s degree en route to the doctoral degree.
  7. A scientific writing sample is required.
  8. Official transcripts are required.
  9. Applicants must provide a CV or résumé.
  10. A statement of professional and career plans is required.
  11. Three letters of recommendation are required.
  12. GRE scores are not required.
  13. International applicants should review the additional requirements applicable to applicants from outside the United States.
  14. Applicants submitting from another time zone should account for Penn State’s Eastern Standard Time zone.

Contact for Application Questions

Applicants who have questions about the application process can contact the HDFS academic programme coordinator.

Applicants with questions about whether GRE scores would strengthen their application or other questions about improving their application may also contact the HDFS Admissions Committee.

Conclusion

The Penn State Human Development and Family Studies Ph.D. programme provides an opportunity for applicants seeking advanced graduate education and research training in the behavioral sciences and related areas.

The programme follows a doctoral pathway, and students entering with a bachelor’s degree are required to complete a master’s degree en route to the Ph.D. Applicants must submit their applications through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal and provide the required academic and supporting materials.

The application requires a scientific writing sample, official transcripts, a CV or résumé, a statement of professional and career plans and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required, and applications are evaluated through a holistic review process.

Interested applicants should begin preparing their application materials early and ensure that their complete application is submitted by the December 1 deadline, taking Penn State’s Eastern Standard Time zone into account.

item.content:encoded:
The University for Peace (UPEACE) Somalia has opened admissions for its 2026 academic enrolment, providing an opportunity for students and professionals from Somalia, East Africa and other parts of the world to pursue postgraduate studies in peace, governance, development, sustainability, humanitarian action, law, human rights and related fields.

The 2026 admissions include a range of Master’s and Doctoral programmes delivered online, making the programmes accessible to applicants who may be unable to relocate for their studies.

In addition to the academic programmes, UPEACE Somalia has announced special scholarship opportunities that can significantly reduce tuition costs for successful applicants. The available scholarships include discounts of up to 30% for Master’s programmes, 50% for PhD programmes and 60% for UPEACE alumni.

The scholarship deadline is 15 September 2026.

About UPEACE Somalia

The University for Peace Somalia was established in 2018 as part of efforts to provide advanced academic programmes that respond to Somalia’s development and peacebuilding needs.

The institution is associated with the University for Peace, which was established in 1980 through United Nations General Assembly Resolution 35/55. The University for Peace is headquartered in Costa Rica and focuses on education and research related to peace, conflict resolution, sustainable development and international cooperation.

UPEACE Somalia provides programmes designed to equip students with knowledge and skills relevant to some of the major challenges facing Somalia, East Africa and the wider international community.

The programmes are offered online and are open to students from Somalia, East Africa and beyond.

UPEACE Somalia 2026 Doctoral Programmes

Applicants interested in pursuing doctoral-level studies can choose from several programmes covering peace, governance, leadership, sustainable development, maritime security and environmental challenges.

The available Doctoral programmes include:

1. Doctoral Programme in Peace, Governance and Development

This programme focuses on the relationship between peace, governance and sustainable development. It is particularly relevant to individuals interested in research and professional work addressing conflict, governance systems, development challenges and peacebuilding.

2. Doctoral Programme in Leadership and Sustainable Development

This programme explores leadership and its role in promoting sustainable development. It may be relevant to professionals and researchers interested in leadership, development policy and long-term approaches to addressing social and economic challenges.

3. Doctoral Programme in Blue Economy and Maritime Security

The programme focuses on issues surrounding the sustainable use of marine resources and maritime security.

It may be particularly relevant to applicants interested in the blue economy, maritime governance, environmental sustainability and security.

4. Doctoral Programme in Land Degradation and Desertification

This programme addresses environmental challenges associated with land degradation and desertification.

It is particularly relevant to research and development priorities in regions affected by drought, environmental degradation and changing climate conditions.

UPEACE Somalia 2026 Master’s Programmes

Applicants seeking Master’s-level study can choose from several programmes covering peace, development, environment, international law, humanitarian action, energy and water resources.

The available Master’s programmes include:

1. Master of Arts in Peace, Governance and Development

This programme combines peace studies with governance and development, providing an opportunity for students to develop knowledge relevant to conflict prevention, peacebuilding, governance and development policy.

2. Master of Arts in Environment, Development and Peace

This programme brings together environmental issues, development and peace. It is relevant to individuals interested in the links between environmental challenges, sustainable development and peacebuilding.

3. Master of Arts in International Law and Human Rights

This programme focuses on international legal frameworks and human rights.

It may be suitable for applicants seeking advanced knowledge of international law, human rights protection and related areas of policy and practice.

4. Master of Arts in Disaster Resilience and Humanitarian Action

This programme focuses on disaster resilience and humanitarian responses.

It is particularly relevant to individuals working or intending to work in humanitarian assistance, disaster management, resilience building and emergency response.

5. Master of Science in Energy, Economics and Governance

This programme examines the relationship between energy, economics and governance.

It provides an opportunity for students interested in energy policy, economic development, governance and sustainable energy systems.

6. Master of Arts in Sustainable Water Resources Management

This programme focuses on the sustainable management of water resources.

It is relevant to applicants interested in water governance, environmental sustainability, development and the management of water resources.

UPEACE Somalia Scholarship Opportunities 2026

One of the major features of the 2026 admissions announcement is the availability of special scholarship opportunities.

According to the announcement, the scholarship opportunities include:

  • 30% scholarships for Master’s programmes.
  • 50% scholarships for PhD programmes.
  • 60% scholarships for UPEACE alumni.

These scholarships can help reduce the financial cost of postgraduate education for eligible applicants.

Applicants should carefully review the scholarship conditions and admission requirements before submitting their applications.

UPEACE Somalia 2026 Admission Requirements

Applicants for the Doctoral programmes are required to have a certified Master’s degree and transcripts, in addition to other requirements that may apply during the application process.

For the Master’s programmes, applicants are required to have a certified Bachelor’s degree and transcripts, alongside any additional requirements specified by UPEACE Somalia.

Applicants should ensure that their academic documents are properly prepared and certified where required before beginning the application process.

Additional admission requirements may vary depending on the selected programme.

Who Can Apply?

The UPEACE Somalia 2026 admissions are open to applicants from Somalia, East Africa and beyond.

The programmes are therefore relevant to prospective postgraduate students from different countries who meet the academic requirements for their selected programme.

Applicants should confirm the specific requirements for their chosen Master’s or Doctoral programme before applying.

Study Format

The programmes offered through UPEACE Somalia are delivered online.

This provides students with an opportunity to pursue postgraduate education without necessarily relocating to another country for their studies.

The online format may be particularly useful for working professionals, researchers and students who need to combine their studies with professional or other responsibilities.

Why Consider UPEACE Somalia?

UPEACE Somalia’s programmes are focused on areas that are closely connected to major development, peace and sustainability challenges.

Depending on the programme selected, students can pursue advanced studies in areas such as:

  • Peacebuilding and conflict transformation
  • Governance and development
  • Sustainable development
  • Environmental management
  • International law
  • Human rights
  • Humanitarian action
  • Disaster resilience
  • Energy governance
  • Water resources management
  • Blue economy
  • Maritime security
  • Land degradation and desertification

These fields can be relevant to careers in government, international organisations, development agencies, humanitarian organisations, research institutions, civil society and other sectors.

Application Deadline

The scholarship deadline for the UPEACE Somalia 2026 admissions is:

15 September 2026

Applicants interested in benefiting from the announced scholarship opportunities should ensure that they submit their applications and complete any required steps before the stated deadline.

How to Apply for UPEACE Somalia 2026

Interested applicants should access the UPEACE Somalia admissions platform to review the available programmes, admission requirements and application procedures.

Applicants should:

  1. Review the available Master’s and Doctoral programmes.
  2. Select a programme that matches their academic background and career interests.
  3. Check the specific admission requirements for the selected programme.
  4. Prepare the required academic documents, including certified degrees and transcripts where applicable.
  5. Review the available scholarship opportunities and their conditions.
  6. Submit the application through the official admissions platform.
  7. Complete any additional steps requested by UPEACE Somalia.

Applicants can also contact UPEACE Somalia through the contact details provided by the institution for enquiries regarding admissions and scholarships.

Conclusion

The UPEACE Somalia 2026 admissions provide an opportunity for students and professionals from Somalia, East Africa and beyond to pursue postgraduate education in fields related to peace, governance, development, sustainability, humanitarian action, international law and environmental management.

With Master’s and Doctoral programmes available online, the opportunity can provide greater flexibility for applicants seeking advanced academic qualifications while remaining in their home countries or continuing their professional activities.

The availability of scholarships further increases the potential accessibility of these programmes, with the announcement indicating 30% scholarships for Master’s programmes, 50% scholarships for PhD programmes and 60% scholarships for UPEACE alumni.

Interested applicants should review the programme-specific requirements and submit their applications before the 15 September 2026 scholarship deadline.
